claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation can form a thin, continuous, adherent oxide layer on a FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The pre-formed oxide will be enriched in readily oxidizable elements such as Cr and Cu.
Pre-oxidation will increase the high-temperature wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Pre-oxidation will make microscopic deformation during sliding more homogeneous.
The oxide layer acts as a load-bearing tribolayer.
The oxide tribolayer reduces local stress concentrations during sliding.
A mildly oxidizing anneal at approximately 700°C can produce the desired nanoscale oxide film.
The continuous oxide reduces direct metal-metal contact during sliding.
Reduced friction-induced stress concentrations suppress severe strain localization in the coating.
Suppression of strain localization promotes more uniform plastic deformation in the underlying alloy.
Preferential wear of the protective oxide rather than the underlying coating reduces overall material loss.
Relative to an untreated coating, the pre-oxidized coating will have lower wear volume at 600–800°C.
Relative to an untreated coating, the pre-oxidized coating will have an improved friction coefficient at 600–800°C.
Relative to an untreated coating, the pre-oxidized coating will exhibit smaller and more evenly distributed plastic-deformation zones.
The protective mechanism operates at 600–800°C when the oxide remains stable.
At lower temperatures or in environments that do not favor oxide formation, the proposed mechanism may not be active.
